manufacturers.short_history: Vektor is the Sverdlovsk production enterprise, today Yekaterinburg, where the Polivoks was developed. Work began in 1980 after management put synthesizer research into the plan; the chief engineer was Vladimir Kuzmin and the instrument's severe military-radio appearance came from his wife Olimpiada Kuzmina. Vektor is a manufacturing enterprise in its own right rather than a design bureau, and the Kachkanar radio factory Formanta, which built the Polivoks in series from 1983 until 1990, was its subsidiary. The plant traded earlier as Electroavtomatika.
conflicts: status: no source says whether the enterprise still trades. 'active' is the column default, not a finding, and must not be read as one.
manufacturers.review_note: Scope question resolved: petelin.ru names it OAO Uralskoye proizvodstvennoye predpriyatiye Vektor (JSC Ural Production Enterprise Vektor), a production enterprise, and describes Formanta in Kachkanar as its subsidiary. It is therefore not a design house that never built anything -- the earlier doubt is settled and it stays. Also: the Polivoks was PLANNED for series production in 1982 but actually started in 1983 (petelin.ru); two dates, two events, not a source conflict. The exact legal name rests on one source, so the canonical name is left as Vektor with the full form recorded in name_history.
